integrated_description: Emma and Alex engage in a structured dialogue to establish specific, measurable boundaries around the ex-girlfriend friendship, including: defined contact parameters (frequency and nature of one-on-one time, avoidance of high-risk contexts such as late-night or alcohol-involved settings), explicit emotional exclusivity standards (the ex may not function as a primary emotional outlet or alternate partner), and a concrete transparency protocol (no hidden direct messages, proactive sharing of relevant interactions without requiring exhaustive disclosure). The couple schedules formal check-ins every 30–60 days beginning with an initial 4–8 week review to assess whether agreements are reducing Emma's anxiety and preserving Alex's autonomy, with the mutual understanding that non-compliance triggers mandatory renegotiation rather than silent resentment, and that repeated or good-faith violations escalate progressively up to and including reduced contact or, as a genuine last resort, distancing from the friendship. All boundaries are designed to protect the couple's emotional fidelity and the dignity of all parties, functioning as safety agreements rather than control mechanisms.
integration_rationale: All three stakeholders converged on the same structural demands—measurable behavioral standards, a transparency protocol, time-bound review, and a graduated consequence-and-escalation path—making full integration achievable without trade-offs; the only variation was in framing (dignity protections from stakeholder_b, last-resort framing from stakeholder_c, resentment-prevention emphasis from stakeholder_a), all of which are preserved in the unified description.
